note: Earliest evidence of agriculture in the subcontinent: Mehrgarh. Taught in the mehrgarh section (NCERT VI fess102 p. 18: among the first places where barley and wheat were grown and sheep and goats reared; one of the earliest villages) and flagged in its exam_note box as a repeated WBCS question.

Earliest evidence of settled agriculture in the subcontinent: Mehrgarh (options Utnur, Burzahom, Mehrgarh, Bagor). Taught in the mehrgarh section; the exam_note separates Mehrgarh (earliest) from Burzahom (also Neolithic, but later and known for pit-houses).

Earliest fossil remains of archaic Homo sapiens: Narmada valley (Hathnora). NOT taught. NCERT VI Ch. 2 (fess102), the chapter's NCERT base, mentions no human fossil. The fact is recorded in the e-PG Pathshala module 'Lower Palaeolithic Culture' (fetched 2026-11-19: the only fossilised cranium in India, from Hathnora on the Narmada river in Madhya Pradesh), but e-PG Pathshala / IGNOU URLs are rejected by books.validate.js for the History profile (sources must be NCERT or WBBSE), so the claim could not be cited in this chapter. Source gap, disclosed in REPORT.md; nothing in the chapter contradicts the official key.
